transcript: Okay, let me try that again, I rushed the first one. So, the disagreement was with my colleague Thu about who owned a lead. A logistics company came in through our website, which that month was her territory, but I'd met their operations director at a trade fair a few weeks earlier and had already sent him a proposal outline. So we both had a real claim. At first I just argued my side, and honestly that went nowhere. What changed it was, I asked her what she was worried about, and it wasn't really the commission, it was that her website numbers were how she got reviewed. That made sense to me. So we went to our manager together, not separately, with a proposal. I'd run the relationship because I knew the director, she'd get the lead credited to her website target, and we'd split the commission. The client got one clear contact person. We closed it about six weeks later. And then we suggested the team write a simple rule for ownership, based on the first logged contact. Thu and I actually ended up sharing a few more accounts after that.
